subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Pipes and cisterns — fill time, drain time, leaks, alternating pipes, rotations

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B fills it in 18 hours. Both pipes are opened together. In how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Rate A = 1/12, Rate B = 1/18. Combined = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 per hour. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 hours = 7 hours 12 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours. Pipe B drains it in 9 hours. If both are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/6 − 1/9 = 3/18 − 2/18 = 1/18 per hour. Tank fills in 18 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 hours. What fraction of the tank will be filled in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: In 5 hours, fraction filled = 5/20 = 1/4.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours and pipe B fills it in 12 hours. Both are opened together for 2 hours, after which A is closed. How many more hours does B take to fill the rest of the tank?
questions.explanation: In 2 hours, A+B fill = 2(1/8 + 1/12) = 2 × 5/24 = 5/12. Remaining = 7/12. B's rate = 1/12. Time for B = (7/12) ÷ (1/12) = 7 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: An inlet pipe fills a tank in 15 hours. A drain empties the full tank in 10 hours. If both are accidentally left open, in how many hours will the full tank become empty?
questions.explanation: Net drain rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 3/30 − 2/30 = 1/30 per hour. A full tank empties in 30 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 36 hours and 45 hours respectively. If both are opened together, what fraction of the tank is filled in 5 hours?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a cistern in 10 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom, it takes 12 hours to fill. In how many hours will the leak alone empty the full cistern?
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/10 − 1/12 = 6/60 − 5/60 = 1/60 per hour. Leak alone empties in 60 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and pipe B fills it in 15 hours. How long will it take to fill the tank if both are opened together?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 per hour. Time = 6 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tap fills 1/3 of a tank in 2 hours. How long will it take the same tap to fill the complete tank?
questions.explanation: Rate = (1/3) ÷ 2 = 1/6 per hour. Full tank takes 6 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 40 minutes. What fraction of the tank is filled in 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: Fraction filled = 10/40 = 1/4.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together fill a tank in 12 hours. Pipe A alone fills it in 20 hours. In how many hours will pipe B alone fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe P can fill a tank in 16 hours and pipe Q in 48 hours. P is opened first and works alone for 6 hours, after which P is closed and Q opens. How many hours does Q take to fill the remaining tank?
questions.explanation: P fills in 6 hours: 6/16 = 3/8. Remaining = 5/8. Time for Q = (5/8) ÷ (1/48) = (5/8) × 48 = 30 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two identical pipes each fill a tank in 30 minutes. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/30 + 1/30 = 2/30 = 1/15 per minute. Time = 15 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tank has a capacity of 480 litres. An inlet pipe fills at 30 litres per minute while an outlet drains at 10 litres per minute. How long will it take to fill the empty tank with both pipes open?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 30 − 10 = 20 litres per minute. Time = 480 ÷ 20 = 24 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 4 hours. After 1 hour, what fraction of the tank remains unfilled?
questions.explanation: In 1 hour A fills 1/4. Unfilled fraction = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A, B, and C fill a tank in 12, 18, and 36 hours respectively, while pipe C (drain) empties it in 36 hours. Actually, pipe C here is an outlet. All three — inlet A, inlet B, and outlet C — are opened together. How long does the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/18 − 1/36 = 3/36 + 2/36 − 1/36 = 4/36 = 1/9 per hour. Tank fills in 9 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A, B, and C can fill a tank in 6, 8, and 12 hours respectively. All three are opened together. After 2 hours, C is closed. How many more hours are needed to fill the rest of the tank?
questions.explanation: In 2 hours, A+B+C fill = 2×(1/6 + 1/8 + 1/12) = 2×9/24 = 3/4. Remaining = 1/4. Rate of A+B = 1/6 + 1/8 = 7/24. Wait — rechecking: need rate of A+B after C closes. A+C together: 1/6+1/12=3/12=1/4. Time for remaining 1/4 = (1/4)÷(1/4)=1 hour.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 hours. Pipe B fills it in 30 hours. A works alone for the first 5 hours, then both A and B work together until the tank is full. What is the total time taken?
questions.explanation: A fills in 5 hours = 5/20 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 per hour. Time for 3/4 = (3/4)÷(1/12) = 9 hours. Total = 5 + 9 = 14 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes fill a tank in 12 and 16 hours. A drain empties it in 24 hours. All three are opened together. How long to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/16 − 1/24 = 4/48 + 3/48 − 2/48 = 5/48 per hour. Time = 48/5 = 9.6 hours = 9 hours 36 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. A hole develops so that with the pipe open the tank now fills in 10 hours instead. How long will the hole alone take to empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: Hole rate = 1/6 − 1/10 = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15 per hour. Hole alone empties in 15 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills 1/4 of a tank in 2 hours. Pipe B fills 1/3 of the same tank in 2 hours. Working together, how long will they take to fill the full tank?
questions.explanation: Rate A = (1/4)/2 = 1/8 per hour. Rate B = (1/3)/2 = 1/6 per hour. Combined = 1/8 + 1/6 = 3/24 + 4/24 = 7/24. Time = 24/7 hours ≈ 3 hours 26 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes fill a tank in 12 and 16 hours. A drain empties it in 8 hours. All three are opened simultaneously. How long will it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/16 − 1/8 = 4/48 + 3/48 − 6/48 = 1/48 per hour (net fill). The tank fills in 48 hours. The drain is powerful but the two inlets together still exceed it.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlet A fills a 300-litre tank in 20 minutes; inlet B fills it in 25 minutes; outlet C drains at 12 litres per minute. All three operate together. How long to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Rate A = 300/20 = 15 L/min; Rate B = 300/25 = 12 L/min; Drain C = 12 L/min. Net = 15 + 12 − 12 = 15 L/min. Time = 300/15 = 20 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 15 and 20 hours respectively. They open alternately, each for 1 hour, starting with A. How many hours will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Per 2-hour cycle (A then B): 1/15 + 1/20 = 4/60 + 3/60 = 7/60. After 8 cycles (16 hours): 8 × 7/60 = 56/60 = 14/15. Remaining = 1/15. In the 17th hour A opens: rate = 1/15 per hour, exactly filling the remaining 1/15. Total = 17 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A, B, and C fill a tank in 6, 9, and 18 hours. All three open together for 2 hours, then B is closed. How much additional time is needed to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 'a' hours and pipe B fills it in 'b' hours. If both are opened together, the time to fill the tank is:
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/a + 1/b = (a+b)/(ab). Time = ab/(a+b). This is the standard formula for two pipes working together.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pump fills a tank in 3 hours. A hole develops and, with the pump running, the tank now fills in 7.5 hours. How long would the hole alone take to empty a full tank?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate with hole = 1/7.5 = 2/15 per hour. Hole rate = 1/3 − 2/15 = 5/15 − 2/15 = 3/15 = 1/5. The hole alone empties the tank in 5 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank 3 times as fast as pipe B. Together they fill the tank in 36 minutes. How long does pipe A take alone?
questions.explanation: Let B fill in x minutes. A fills in x/3 minutes. Together: 3/x + 1/x = 4/x = 1/36. So x = 144 minutes. A alone = 144/3 = 48 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B, C fill a tank. C takes 56 hours, B fills twice as fast as C, and A fills twice as fast as B. How long do all three together take?
questions.explanation: C fills in 56 hr, B in 28 hr, A in 14 hr. Combined rate = 1/56 + 1/28 + 1/14 = 1/56 + 2/56 + 4/56 = 7/56 = 1/8. Together: 8 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A cistern is 1/4 full. Drain B (empties in 6 hours) opens first. After 1 hour, inlet A (fills in 4 hours) also opens. How many total hours from the start until the cistern is completely full?
questions.explanation: After 1 hour of B alone: 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12. Now A+B open: net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 per hour (filling). Need to reach 1 from 1/12: remaining = 11/12. Time = (11/12)÷(1/12) = 11 hours. Total = 1 + 11 = 12 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 5 hours. When pipe A and drain D are both open, the tank fills in 10 hours. How long does drain D alone take to empty the full tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (10 hr) and B (15 hr) alternate, each open for 1 hour, starting with A. How many hours to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Per 2-hr cycle: 1/10+1/15 = 1/6. After 5 cycles (10 hr): 5/6. Remaining = 1/6. Hour 11 (A): fills 1/10, total = 5/6+1/10 = 28/30 = 14/15. Remaining = 1/15. Hour 12 (B): fills 1/15, exactly finishing. Total = 12 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in p hours. With a leak, it fills in q hours (q > p). The time for the leak alone to empty the full tank is:
questions.explanation: Leak rate = 1/p − 1/q = (q−p)/(pq). Time = pq/(q−p). Note: since q > p, the denominator is positive and the formula gives a valid positive time.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tank holds 800 litres. An inlet fills at 30 L/min and a drain empties at 6 L/min. Both are open. How long (in minutes) to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 30 − 6 = 24 L/min. Time = 800/24 = 100/3 minutes ≈ 33 minutes 20 seconds.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes X (20 min) and Y (30 min) both fill a tank. Y is closed 10 minutes before the tank is full. Find the total time taken to fill the tank.
questions.explanation: Let total time = T. X runs T minutes, Y runs (T−10) minutes. T/20 + (T−10)/30 = 1. Multiply by 60: 3T + 2(T−10) = 60 → 5T = 80 → T = 16 minutes. Check: X fills 16/20 = 4/5; Y fills 6/30 = 1/5. Sum = 1. ✓
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 9 hours. Drain B empties it in 18 hours. A is opened first. After 3 hours B is also opened. How many more hours after B opens does the tank take to be full?
questions.explanation: A fills in 3 hours: 3/9 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3. With A+B open: net rate = 1/9 − 1/18 = 2/18 − 1/18 = 1/18 per hour. Time = (2/3)÷(1/18) = 12 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: An inlet fills a tank in 10 hours. An outlet drains at exactly half the inlet's rate. If both are open together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Inlet rate = 1/10 per hour. Outlet = half of inlet = 1/20. Net = 1/10 − 1/20 = 1/20. Tank fills in 20 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlet A fills a tank in 6 hours. Drain C empties it in 4 hours. Only A and C are open, and the tank starts full. How long until the tank is completely empty?
questions.explanation: Net drain rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12 per hour. A full tank empties in 12 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A is 3/2 times as efficient as pipe B. Together they fill a tank in 15 hours. How long does pipe A take alone?
questions.explanation: Let B fill in x hours. A is 3/2 times as efficient → A fills in (2/3)x hours. Together: 3/(2x) + 1/x = 5/(2x) = 1/15, so 2x = 75, x = 37.5. A alone = (2/3) × 37.5 = 25 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours. Due to a hole, the effective fill time increases to 18 hours. How long would the hole alone take to empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: Hole rate = 1/12 − 1/18 = 3/36 − 2/36 = 1/36 per hour. The hole alone drains the full tank in 36 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A (4 hr) opens at 8:00 AM, pipe B (6 hr) opens at 9:00 AM, and pipe C (12 hr) opens at 10:00 AM. At what time will the empty tank be full?
questions.explanation: Let tank fill at t hours after 8 AM. A runs t hr, B runs (t−1) hr, C runs (t−2) hr. Equation: t/4 + (t−1)/6 + (t−2)/12 = 1. Multiply by 12: 3t + 2(t−1) + (t−2) = 12 → 6t − 4 = 12 → t = 8/3 hr = 2 hr 40 min. Full at 8:00 + 2:40 = 10:40 AM. Check: A fills 2/3, B fills 5/18, C fills 1/18; sum = 12/18+5/18+1/18 = 1. ✓
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (6 hr) and B (8 hr) fill a tank. Drain C is also open. When all three operate together the tank fills in 24 hours. How long does drain C alone take to empty the full tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlet A fills a tank in 16 hours; drain B empties it in 12 hours. Both are open simultaneously and the tank starts 3/4 full. How long before the tank is completely empty?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/16 − 1/12 = 3/48 − 4/48 = −1/48 per hour (net drain at 1/48 per hr). Time to drain 3/4: (3/4)÷(1/48) = 36 hours.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Three pipes A (10 hr), B (12 hr), and drain C (8 hr) rotate — each open for exactly 1 hour in the sequence A→B→C→A→... Starting from an empty tank, how long does it take to fill?
questions.explanation: Per 3-hr rotation: 1/10 + 1/12 − 1/8 = 12/120 + 10/120 − 15/120 = 7/120. After 17 complete rotations (51 hr): 17×7/120 = 119/120. Remaining = 1/120. Next hour is A's turn (rate = 1/10 = 12/120 per hr). Time for 1/120 = (1/120)÷(12/120) = 1/12 hr = 5 min. Total = 51 hr 5 min.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in (x+5) hours. Together they fill the tank in 6 hours. Find the value of x (hours for pipe A alone).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlet A fills in 30 min, inlet B fills in 40 min, drain C empties at some rate. All three open for 10 minutes, then C is closed and A+B finish in 8 more minutes (18 min total). How long does drain C take alone to empty the full tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlets A (8 hr) and B (12 hr) plus drain C (6 hr) are all open. After t hours the drain is closed and A+B continue. The tank fills in exactly 12 hours total. Find t.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlets A (20 hr), B (30 hr), and drain C (15 hr) all operate together. How long to fill the empty tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/15 = 3/60 + 2/60 − 4/60 = 1/60. The tank fills in 60 hours. The drain is large but both inlets combined exceed it by 1/60 per hour.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe normally fills a tank in 12 hours. A clog reduces its efficiency by 25%. Simultaneously a leak develops that drains at 1/3 of the pipe's original rate. How long now to fill the empty tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tank holds 1800 litres. Inlet A flows at 60 L/min and inlet B at 40 L/min; drain C removes 50 L/min. In the first t minutes only A and C are open; then all three run together until full. The total fill time is 42 minutes. Find t.
questions.explanation: Phase 1 (t min, A+C): net = 60−50 = 10 L/min → fills 10t litres. Phase 2 ((42−t) min, A+B+C): net = 60+40−50 = 50 L/min → fills 50(42−t) litres. Total = 1800: 10t + 50(42−t) = 1800 → 10t + 2100 − 50t = 1800 → −40t = −300 → t = 7.5 minutes.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
